## Verdict

Kelp costs least for a team of 8, at $168 per month. Despite the highest per-seat rate on the list, its 1-seat minimum means the team pays for exactly 8 seats. Acme Desk and Fennel HQ both have minimums well above 8, so their low headline rates are irrelevant at this size.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $11 | 20 |
| Fennel HQ | $15 | 40 |
| Kelp | $21 | 1 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (8) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Kelp:** minimum 1 is below 8, so 8 seats paid. 8 × $21 = **$168 per month**.
- **Acme Desk:** minimum 20 exceeds 8, so 20 seats paid. 20 × $11 = **$220 per month**. Twelve unused seats, worth $132.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 40 exceeds 8, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Thirty-two unused seats, worth $480.

Kelp is $52 per month cheaper than Acme Desk and $432 cheaper than Fennel HQ — $624 and $5,184 over twelve months.

## Risks

This ranking is unusually fragile, because Kelp wins on minimums while losing badly on rate. Acme Desk's $220 is fixed until 20 seats; at 11 people it already costs the same as Kelp ($231 versus $220), and beyond that Acme Desk is cheaper at every size. A team expecting to pass 10 people within the contract term should price Acme Desk instead.

Fennel HQ only reaches its list rate at 40 seats, where it costs $600 against Kelp's $840 — so it too overtakes Kelp eventually, just much later.

The price list carries nothing on features, support, limits or contract terms, so this is a price comparison and not a recommendation on fit. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments or negotiated discounts are not covered and could reorder the result.
